f'(x)=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(22 x^{\frac{3}{2}} - 22 x^{2}\right)=33 \sqrt{x} - 44 x
$$

We then compute $f'(1)$, which gives

$$
m=f'(1)=-11=-11
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line ${m}^{′}$ is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{\left(-11\right)}=\frac{1}{11}.
$$

$$
f'(x)=6 x + 9
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(-1,-6):$

$$
m=f'(-1)=3=3
$$

Therefore, the slope ${m}^{'}$ of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{\left(3\right)}=- \frac{1}{3}.
$$
